result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers fully satisfy every rubric item with specific, usable fixes. Answer A is stronger overall because it adds semantic table markup, action names that include the user, an explicit warning that :focus-within still leaves out touch, and a concrete CSS sketch for type size, right alignment, tabular figures, and row rules. Answer B matches the core recommendations and adds useful product notes such as invited status, undo, and a clear priority list. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers cover all five recommendations at the same depth and in the same order: right-aligned tabular figures, light row rules with padding or zebra striping, 13–14px body text, row actions that stay available without hover, and a clear Never (or explained dash) for missing last logins. A adds admin-workflow detail such as invited status, confirmation or undo, and sorting those users. B adds a ready CSS sketch, semantic table markup, and action names that include the user. Those extras sit outside the rubric and do not separate the two answers.
